Principle:
Spirit, mind, the living being.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ The will to live, urge to rule, striving for an objective, organization, ability to make a decision. - Lack of vitality and willpower, lack of determination and organization, indecision or vacillation.

Biological Correspondence:
Health, vitality, heart, circulation. The body, cells.

Sociological Correspondence:
Man, father, authority, leading personality, official, civil servant.

Position in Houses and Signs:
T 0014 I Storming and urging nature, leading nature or character, urge to do something, consciousness of purpose or objective, enthusiasm, courage, boldness and audacity, passion, urge to rule or lust for power, quarrelsome. Advancement in life partly through ruthlessness. Difficulties through hastiness. G 0015 II Rich soul life, perseverance, endurance, constructiveness, sense of form, humor, material outlook, practical nature, love of pleasure and enjoyment. Money matters are often important. Striving for secure circumstances in life. X00\6 III Vivacious, joy of life, versatile, adaptable, restless, superficial, eagerness to learn or study, the faculty to absorb or grasp a subject, love of change, fluctuating inclinations. S0017 IV Wealth of feeling, joy of marriage, connubial love, receptive, impressionable, benevolent, contemplative nature, reserved, domestic, love of comfort, harmonious family life. Ups and downs in life. 0018 V Domineering people, self-confidence, formative energy, creativity, self-assured, striving for possessions, wealth of ideas, organization, leadership, rise and advancement in life through one's own ability, patronage and protection. TIP 0019 VI Care and diligence or attention, orderliness, correctness, sense of criticism, methodical mind, analytical ability, simplicity, contentment. Enmity caused through fault-finding. Extensive studies. Good opportunities are often missed. ^ 0020 VII Harmony, public spirit, sociable, adaptable, vanity, the desire to be a person of importance, love of the arts, good manners. Lack of firmness, consistency, constancy. Associations are important. Til 0021 VIII People with willpower. The struggle for existence, the power to succeed and to maintain one's position in life, tenacity, over-estimation of self, excessive passion, fearlessness, fanaticism. Quarrels, difficulties caused through one's own fault or attitude. / 0022 IX Mobility, readiness for action, love of sport, generosity, idealism, enthusiasm. Sociable, changeable mood, dual nature. Striving for a secure position in life, slow advancement, important associations. ^ 0023 X Hard-working. Concentration upon the self, a serious outlook on life, tenacious clinging to one's goal or aspiration in life, tenacity or toughness, industrious, a sense of reality. Rise and advancement through untiring effort, vocational interests are of primary importance. ss 0024 XI Good powers of observation, intuitive understanding of other people, adaptable, mutable, ready to help others, sociable, knowledge of human nature, a sympathetic attitude toward new ways or methods. Rebellion against tutelage or restriction. Rise and advancement through one's effort, but also through help coming from others. K 0025 XII Reserve, receptivity, the faculty to absorb, moodiness, patience, negligence, love of comfort, a secretive nature. Restrictions in life caused through inner inhibitions, difficulties caused through a negative attitude.

Soul, the female principle.

Principle:
Intellect, mediation.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Good grasp or understanding of a subject, sound judgement, critical ability, dexterity in expression and writing, mediation, diplomacy, general intellectual abilities, analysis. - A lack of understanding and of objective criticism, tendency to diffuse one's energy into too many channels, inhibitions in speech and writing, over-development or weakness of intellect.

Biological Correspondence:
The motor nerves (speech and hearing organs).

Sociological Correspondence:
Intellectual workers, trades-people, agents or mediators.

Position in Houses and Signs:
T 0040 I Mental activity, constructive intellect, creative thinking, keen powers of observation, criticism, enthusiasm, quickness at repartee in speech and writing, rashness, exaggeration, mental overwork. Nervous. 0 0041 II Logical thinking, formal thinking, logic, endurance and patience in relation to mental activity, a sense of form, deliberation. One-sided views. Hoarseness caused by too much talking. X 0042 III Versatile thinking, love of variety and change, adaptable, business talent. Lack of constancy, honesty, tidiness. Active or lively correspondence. S 0043 IV Perception, interrelationship between thinking and feeling, good memory, tendency to become deeply immersed in something, positive or constructive criticism, one's own individual methods of work, a sense of harmony, art interests. ^ 0044 V Creative thinking, power of enthusiasm, wealth of plans, organizing ability, prudence, far-sightedness, speculation, desire for possessions. Intellectual leaders, organizers, speculators. T\y 0045 VI Thirst for knowledge, practical thinking, patience, well-grounded expert knowledge and specialized skill, little ability to comprehend the whole. Tidiness, care and attention, criticism. Nervous disturbances of the digestive tract owing to a sedentary life. Good collaboration and cooperation, teamwork. ^ 0046 VII Creative thinking within patterns already in existence, teamwork, adaptable, good powers of comparison, sense of justice, sense of form and beauty, good manners, tactful mediation. HI 0047 VIII Sharp criticism, fanaticism, endurance and perseverance in the pursuit of difficult problems and in the solution of arduous tasks, practical ability. Sarcasm, skepticism, cunning and craft. Lively disputes, arguments, fights. / 0048 IX Deep thinking coupled with social or religious tendencies, the philosopher, manifold interests, a striving for justice and truth, occupation with the problems of life. The danger of scattering one's energies. The tendency to evade difficult tasks or to take the line of least resistance. n 0049 X Concentration, thoroughness, endurance, patience, consciousness of aim or objective, logic, tendency to view life seriously, solution of difficult problems. Melancholy, cunning, crafty. Success through one's own merit, economy, reserve. Ambition is often the driving force behind all activity. ss 0050 XI Progressive thinking, interest in inventions and reforms, a wealth of plans, quick grasp of a situation. Individual and original judgement, creative thinking, enthusiasm. Utopian ideas, tendency to revel, desire to work alone. Organizers, reformers, inventors. H 0051 XII A person whose thoughts are easily influenced by others, receptive to the thoughts of others, ability to reproduce, fantasy and imagination. Planning without energy of action, philosophical ideas.

Principle:
Love, art.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Physical attraction, feeling, a sense of harmony, beauty and art, a positive outlook or attitude toward life. - Sexual aberration, sentimentality, a want of taste, heedlessness, vice.

Biological Correspondence:
Glandular products (kidneys, veins).

Sociological Correspondence:
A young girl or maiden, sweetheart or mistress, people who are connected with centers of art or centers of entertainment. Positions in Houses and Signs T 0053 I Ardent and passionate love, the power to wish, reveling or romantic dreaming, the development of creative powers. Desire for change, tendency to involve oneself in love adventures, love at first sight. d 0054 II A deep-seated feeling, strong personal power of attraction, constancy, faithfulness, a conservative character. Love of luxury and of precious stones, artistic interests. X 0055 III All-embracing sympathy, charm, courtesy, cooperative attitude, ability to accommodate oneself to circumstances, desire to discuss ideas with others. Superficial love attachments lead to conflict. S 0056 IV A deep-seated feeling of love, a strong urge to lean on someone, appreciation of family and home, art and music. Digestive troubles are caused by excessive enjoyment of delicacies or tidbits. ft 0057 V A warm heart desiring love and also arousing love easily in the partner. Abundance of love. Enjoyment of social entertainment, pleasure and games. The desire to dress well and to live in an environment of luxury. Quick contacts with other people, often a premature marriage. W 0058 VI Moral sense, the dictates of the heart often suppressed by practical considerations, indecision in matters of love, striving for moral purity. ^ 0059 VII A person who knows how to live, a friendly and obliging manner quickly brings about contacts with other people, the enjoyment of social engagements and pleasures, good taste, artistic skill. The danger of scattering one's affections. TL 0060 VIII Strong powers of attraction, a passionate disposition, vacillation or wavering between the extremes of self-control and licentiousness, fanaticism in love, jealousy, the tendency to waste one's vital energy. The danger of illness from intemperance. <"0061 IX The power to wish, idealistic motives in love life, inclined to romantic imaginings, occasional moodiness, hypersensitivity, instability, the scattering of one's energies. n 0062 X Constancy, faithfulness, a sense of responsibility, self-control in love relationships, attachment to mature partners who have gained experience in life. Jealousy, distrust, obsolete views. Too much self-control and a "matter of fact" manner may bring about the danger of disappointments and separations. ss 0063 XI Modem and progressive views on love relationships, peculiar plans and ideas, enjoyment of social contacts, love of independence, appreciation of modem art forms. Associations through friendship are important. Protection (in the sense of benefits through sponsorship). K 0064 XII Longing for love, subject to emotional and sexual life. Occasional lack of self-control, impressionable, seductible. Carefree nature, comfort, predominating love of music and other artistic activities.

Meetings, alliances, societies, contacts, blood ties, kindred and related people.

Ego-consciousness and spiritual awareness.

The individualized man, the aim of life.

Ego-consciousness, the function of the brain proper.

Fanaticism, rashness, covetousness. 0 0171 Persistent pursuit of one's aims, endurance, slow but sure establishment of one's own personality, striving for secure circumstances in 1 In traditional astrology the Ascendant rather than the MC was always considered of the greatest importance. The interpretation of the MC as "I" was originally introduced by Alfred Witte. In the opinion of the author, the term ego-consciousness is perhaps better. This interpretation was not known or used a few thousand years ago because the ego-consciousness as it is understood today had not then yet developed. More about this can be found in Jean Gebser's Ursprung undGegenwart, Stuttgart 1949. The paintings in the pyramids reveal that the artists at that time did not have any knowledge of perspective. They drew two dimensionally. It was not until the time of Michelangelo that perspective was discovered, as man learned to see in three dimensions. It was through this that man began to realize the distance of things and recognize his own self in contrast to the material world and other people. It was at this time that the real "I-consciousness" developed. Although Christ's "It is I" is often considered as the origin of the "I-experience" as opposed to the former "We-experience." Practical experience has further bom out this interpretation of the MC. In cases of "ego diseases" the MC has been found to be repeatedly involved. (The "ego-diseases" seem to be the result of false or distorted relationships with other people.) life, tolerance. Tendency to be particular and difficult to please in one's desires, mistrust, egotism. £0172 Manifold aims, vigorous striving, periodic creativity, quick but not always permanent establishment of one's own individuality. The tendency to scatter one's energy, superficiality. S 0173 Tactful but emphatic establishment of one's individuality, striving for independence in spite of great consideration for others, simplicity and modesty, thrift. Impressionable, sensitive. 0174 High aspirations, strong urge to climb socially, self-confidence, optimism, generosity, urge to lead, organization. Egotism, pretentious nature, hyper-sensitive in matters of humor. HP 0175 Striving for a secure livelihood and permanent position in life, advancement by simple means, organization, tidiness, critical attitude. Ruthlessness, over-estimation of self, habit of overtaxing one's powers and energy. / 0178 Striving for material security and high standing, great planning power, extension or enlargement in the sphere of thought, growth of the spiritual or inner side of one's nature. Adventurous aspirations, a conservative attitude, urge to be a person of importance or always to be in the limelight, inconstant. "VS 0179 Self-confidence, intense striving for the attainment of one's objectives, slow but sure establishment of one's own personality through industry and endurance, simplicity and modestness, domesticity, a sense of reality. A mania for innovations and novelties, scattering of energies through too much planning. K 0181 Wait-and-see attitude, striving for a simple and easy life with occasional pleasures and periodic seclusion to occupy oneself with philosophical problems. Lack of clarity, impressionable, temporary instability.

native_text:
Principle:
Spirit and soul, the conscious and the unconscious, vitality and feeling, husband and wife.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ A harmonious character, inner balance. - Inner discontent, an unbalanced nature, the struggle between duty and interests or hobbies, tendency to allow inner conflicts to manifest. C There is an appreciable influence of the zodiacal sign in which the conjunction occurs. One-sidedness or one-track mind, the misunderstood person.

Biological Correspondence:
Balance and economy of bodily liquids, serum. The eyes.

Sociological Correspondence:
Husband and wife, father and mother, boyfriend and girlfriend, friend, marriage, the parents, friendship.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Good relationship between parents and partners, making contacts with partners and friends, joint success, having to do with public life. - Disharmony between parents or partners, differences caused by inner tensions, dissatisfaction and the ensuing difficulties. 2 It has been noted that this book omits interpretations of mid-point combinations in which the axis factor is already one of the components of the mid-point. If for example we are considering the mid-point Sun/Moon in a chart neither Sun or Moon can actually occupy the axis. But they can however enter this axis by transit or by direction e.g. Sun = Sun/Moon or Moon = Sun/Moon. This raises the question of whether this combination has any particular value. It would appear that in cases of this kind that the doubled factor comes out more strongly. In the case of Sun = Sun/Moon, one can assume that the Sun factor will be particularly emphasized, bringing out the male, mental side. In the case of Moon = Sun/Moon, it is possible that the Moon factor will predominate accentuating the female, emotional and unconscious side. It should be pointed out again however that the interpretations in this book are not meant to be taken exactly word for word and applied literally without any trouble or consideration. One should always combine the individual factors and interpret the chart as a whole. O/D

Chronic disturbances of water balance in the body, defects of the mucous membrane, wounds secreting liquid deposits, mainly watery ones. Diseases of the bladder, psychical diseases, hereditary diseases.

Moon/Saturn D/h

native_text:
Principle:
Emotional tensions. Sudden manifestation of subconscious forces.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Increased emotional excitability, attentiveness, ambition, tendency to act according to one's instincts, a strong self-will, tendency to strive tor a goal or objective, determination, an unconditional pursuit of one's own conviction, interest in the metaphysical sciences and realms (clairvoyance). - An excessive self-will, stubbornness, fanaticism, tendency to exaggerate or magnify things, inclination to strain the nerves, striving for absolute independence, unrest or restlessness, craving of sensation. C An over-strained emotional life, peculiar interests, intellectual talents, individualism.

Biological Correspondence:
The rhythm of the water economy in the blood, blood pressure disturbances, colic of the water-excreting organs (prostate diseases). Connections with the female period.

Sociological Correspondence:
Restless, nervous or ambitious women, female reformists.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Sacrifices for the attainment of special aims, help and assistance through friends, attainment of sudden success, accomplishment of a change in one's circumstances. - Tendency to overdo things either in work or in the pursuit of objectives strains the nervous system. States of fear and anxiety. 23 Schizophrenic symptoms have been found at times, but one should be careful not to diagnose schizophrenia in the case of every Moon -Uranus aspect. If such a tendency is found there are usually additional factors which are inherited. Moon/Uranus D/W

native_text:
Principle:
Subconscious phenomena, a refined sense of feeling.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Sensitivity, the ability to feel and to understand other people's troubles in a sympathetic manner, inner vision and imaginative perception. Inspiration, far-reaching wishes, vivid dream experiences. - Fanciful imaginings or illusions, self-deception, lack of stability, prone to lying, tendency to gravitate toward low-grade spiritism and mediumistic illusions. C A refined sense of feeling, love of solitude caused by being misunderstood and unsatisfied, a peculiar disposition and strange notions.

Biological Correspondence:
Paralyzed blood circulation, an over-balance or an over-accumulation of water in the tissues of the body, a deficiency of the osmotic functions relating to the utilization of the cell salts (disturbance of consciousness or awareness, also a break in consciousness; eye-diseases).

Sociological Correspondence:
Sensitive persons, impressionable women, weak or feeble persons. Disappointed or disillusioned women. Mediums, people connected with psychical phenomena and investigations, women who tell fortunes by cards or female cartomancers. Probable Manifestation + A sympathetic understanding of other people (psychometry), the activity of the subconscious, a state of relaxation, receptiveness, impressionableness, an intensely vivid dream life. - Danger of being exposed to peculiar and strange influences or being exploited by other people. Instability, weakness and life crises are caused by laziness or indolence. 24 In the case of aspects between Moon and Neptune in a female chart, especially the conjunction, square and opposition, it has been found that there are often difficulties in the relationship with the marriage partner which were found to be due mainly to over-sensitivity, not being understood or a lack of confidence. Moon/Neptune D/V

The metabolism of liquids in the body, diseases of the blood.

People with extreme emotional expression.

The activity of the organs, smooth muscular tissue, heart muscle. The completed birth, the first cry.

A person successful in an enterprise (e.g., a manufacturer or the managing director of a company), capable organizer, propagandists. Learned and educated people, academicians belonging to the legal profession. Jurists or writers on law, civil servants or government officials.

+ Successful enterprise, fortunate business deal or settlement, successful results in one's profession, vocation or occupation. Agreements, contracts, getting engaged, marriage, births. - Resolutions and decisions, settlement of conflicts, clearing the air after disputes or quarrels, rebellion against guardianship or tutelage, marital differences. Mars/Jupiter dVU

native_text:
Principle:
Harmful or destructive energy. Inhibited or destroyed vitality.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Endurance, power of resistance, indefatigable. - Concentrated energy outwardly expressed as violence or inwardly shown as destructive power, hardness, harshness or bitterness, self-willed, obstinate. One's interest in any enterprise or activity lasts only such time as is required for overcoming the main difficulties. C Tendency to be injured, mostly destructive or pernicious forms of energy.

Biological Correspondence:
Bone-forming process, joints, muscles as active factors and bones as passive factors, joining spots of the tendons or sinews with the bones. An inflammation of the bones or of the bone marrow. The death or atrophy of an organ, particularly paralysis of the muscles belonging to the breathing mechanism. (Death through suffocation.)

Sociological Correspondence:
Manual laborers, miners. Energetic people who are able to overcome the greatest difficulties.

Probable Manifestations:
+ The more energy the more difficulties are overcome, or vice versa. - Periods of impotence and weakness alternating with periods of brutal or ruthless progress and advancement in life. All will-directed activity meets complete resistance (as governed by circumstances). Tests of strength, disputes, separations, illnesses. Cases of death. 37 One is inclined at times to consider Mars/Satum as the "death axis." This combination is found in many cases at the time of death, but one should not make the mistake of taking it for granted that death will result. During the course of life this "death axis" is very often stimulated by transits and directions, but life continues. Such periods are often marked by difficulties and illness, difficulties to be overcome or the death of other people. It should also be taken into consideration that life is often prolonged through medical science or new medical equipment through which many people near death are kept alive. Mars/Saturn cT/*?

native_text:
Principle:
A sudden application of effort, a bodily intervention (an operation).

Psychological Correspondence:
+ An extraordinary and unusual amount of energy made available for quite suddenly, urge for freedom and independence, the trait neither to be subdued nor to yield to other people's will, quick determination, courage. - Argumentative disposition, inclination to contradict others, self-will and self-willed obstinacy, lack of balance, intolerance, urge for freedom, strong emotional tensions, strains or stresses, a person imbued with a fighting spirit, violence. C Obstinacy, brutal frankness, self-will and wilfulness, intolerance, haste and premature action, prone to injuries or accidents.

Biological Correspondence:
The rhythm of activity, activity and work of the heart. An injury causing the loss of blood, beginning of an operation (the cutting of the skin), loss of blood. A scar.

Sociological Correspondence:
Violent people, fighters for freedom, revolutionaries.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Unusual achievements through an extraordinary power of effort, inclination to act too hastily or prematurely, a danger or peril which has fortunately passed. - The passing of a test of nerves, struggle for survival, accident, injury, operation (birth). 40 The mid-point Mars/Uranus is often interpreted as the "operation axis" and this has been substantiated both in the case of directions and transits. But one cannot say for certain that these combinations will mean an operation. In cases where an operation is inevitable, other combinations usually must be present. The correspondence "operation" is only one possibility of this combination. Mars/Uranus cW

native_text:
Principle:
Optimism, a lucky chance, blissful realization.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ Desire for knowledge, aspiration for inner perception, good intuition, ability to have fortunate ideas and realize them, organizing ability, the right feeling for everything new, quick grasp of a situation, prudence, farsightedness, philosophical interests. - Love of freedom, urge for independence, obstinate adherence to one's principles from inherent opposition rather than from real conviction, tendency to magnify things or to exaggerate everything, inconstant, tactless. C Urge for independence, zealous representation of one-sided views, conflicts concerning one's philosophy of life or religion.

Biological Correspondence:
The organic rhythm (of life): the peristalsis of the intestines. Spastic (= convulsive) fits or disorders, colic with a time limit, no permanent pain.

Sociological Correspondence:
Organizers, inventors. Adventurers and fortune-hunters.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Fortunate turns in life, sudden change of destiny, sudden recognition, successful speculation. - Tendency to miss the best chances or opportunities and to involve oneself in arguments with others on matters of outlook on life or on questions of life philosophy. N. B. It is often difficult to assess the nature of Jupiter-Uranus constellations. They indicate, in most cases, inner tension or strain which is then suddenly released. At one time, the author named this configuration the "Thank the Lord" position because people having such a configuration have repeatedly exclaimed the words "Thank the Lord" after the release of the tension or strain from which they were suffering. Jupiter/Uranus 4/^

native_text:
Principle:
Elimination of the waking consciousness.

Psychological Correspondence:
+ The development and growth of subconscious powers or forces, inner vision, inner illumination and enlightenment, inspiration, idealism, an interest in spiritual subjects, religious problems, mysticism, art. - Lack of control of the waking consciousness leads to want of clarity. Instability, lack of emotional balance, nervous sensitivity, wrong ideas, one-sidedness. C Extraordinary and unusual inclinations.

Biological Correspondence:
Paralysis of rhythmic processes. Heart failure, apoplexy of the brain. (A still-bom child.)

Sociological Correspondence:
Mystics, people engaged in psychic research, mediums.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Peculiar psychic states, inspiration, spiritual cognition and understanding. Long journeys. (Contacts with foreign countries.) - Lack of stamina and vitality, confused psychic states, peculiar inclinations, losses. 58 Even though the conjunction of Uranus and Neptune does not appear in the charts of the present generation these effects do occur in the case of directions and transits. For rectification of the time of birth it is useful to examine the death of relatives and it often will be found that Uranus/Neptune was in the death axis at the time. In the statistical examination of several hundred still births this configuration was found very frequently. However this also is found in the case of a period of temporary unconsciousness, It is therefore important never to give this interpretation when directions occur stating that death is likely. So often this mid-point occurs in life without the worst happening. We cannot too often stress the importance of being careful in these cases. Uranus/Neptune W/V

native_text:
Principle:
Insecurity, uncertainty. A lack of "ego-consciousness."

Psychological Correspondence:
+ A devotion to far-reaching objectives without being able to bring them to realization. Peculiar ideas, interest in the investigation of the unconscious and the supernatural. - Undefined objectives in life. Insecurity, lack of self-confidence, tendency to succumb to strange and unusual influences. C Aimlessness and a lack of purpose and directive in life, lack of self-confidence.

Biological Correspondence:
Depressive psychoses, mental disturbance. Numbness in limbs.

Sociological Correspondence:
People with Utopian ideas, crooks or swindlers. "Man of big talk but not of action." Weaklings.

Probable Manifestations:
+ Devotion to peculiar objectives, inclination to feign, pose or put on an act. - Pursuit of wrong ideas, prone to deception. 64 Neptune/MC should not always be interpreted negatively but can mean an especially sensitive individual who is particularly sensitive to others, or it can indicate an interest in the occult or in parapsychological problems, e. g., this combination was found in the case of a very well known research worker who occupied himself with parapsychological problems. An aspect of transiting or directed Neptune to the MC can in certain circumstances result in a very deep depression and far-reaching disappointments, reducing the patient to someone who feels incapable of undertaking anything. In the case of transiting Neptune over the MC one must remember that this can occur several times in the course of two years. In a case like this the whole must be considered. Neptune/Medium Coeli V/M

Principle:
Relationship between the ego (higher self) and the lower self (personality).

Psychological Correspondence:
The living being, the individual synthesis, is founded upon the relationship between ego and self. As both the Ascendant and the Medium Coeli are determined mathematically and astronomically, a characterization can only evolve when further configurations have reference to these two points.

Biological Correspondence:
The phenotype in contrast to the combinations Sun/Moon, Moon/Medium Coeli and Dragon's Head/Medium Coeli expressing relationships to the genotype (hereditary factors).

Sociological Correspondence:
The personality as directed by ego-consciousness.

Probable Manifestations:
Connections between the Asc. and the MC when brought out by progressions or transits indicate important periods of life which can be characterized and colored only through the addition and incorporation of other factors. 67 The mid-point AS/MC should always be examined as this, frequently has a bearing on the whole personality and because directions over this point may result in a change of life and circumstances. Ascendant/Medium Coeli A/M

native_text: An obliging person, seeking contacts with other people. New faces in one's environment. General Remarks The observation and research of illness requires a great deal of care and tact. The author has been particularly careful in all of his statements. No-one should be tempted to give a diagnosis on the basis of the cosmic picture alone because it is impossible. So many factors add to the situation which is shown in the chart, but which can only be released under special circumstances. These cannot be foreseen from the chart. One should always consider that Biological Correspondences are based on cooperation with doctors. The Biological Correspondences can become effective through various circumstances. One must always be very careful in interpreting disease. Those who work on cosmobiology must be constantly aware that it is nonsense to read the destiny from the stars alone. It is also important to have some knowledge of psychology and medicine and a rich experience of life if one wants to help not only one's own family but others too. With every word spoken by the cosmoblological investigator one should be conscious of the responsibility and the damaging consequences which the wrong words could have. One does not help others by making them afraid of the future but must use every opportunity to build up their self-confidence and their self-consciousness of their own value. Those who advise others should always remember that it is not for them to bring about a decision in the life of another. It is for the cosmobiologist to give help and build up confidence in others so that they can make their own decisions to the best of their ability. Translator's Notes Since the appearance of the first English edition in 1960, The Combination of Stellar Influences has universally established itself as a standard work of outstanding importance. In preparing this translation of the 1961 supplement we have followed Dr. Roosedale's translation of technical terms wherever appropriate, e.g., "Gestim" has been translated as "stellar body" to refer equally to planet, Sun or Moon. Likewise, quotations from the main body of the text have always been given as they appear in the original translation. As many readers may be as yet unfamiliar with the 90o-circle method of charting described in this supplement, it should be mentioned that this method is usually employed in conjunction with a 90o-dial. This is a simple instrument which enables one to examine all the mid-point axes in a chart in a few minutes. It is an absolutely essential tool for work in this field. Meanwhile it is hoped that this supplementary material will further stimulate research along the lines pioneered by Mr, Ebertin. Charles Harvey Use Hodges May 1969 It has always been the intention that the individual statements given in The Combination of Stellar Influences should only be used as suggestions for the interpretation of the combinations and never as though they were immutable and finally established rules. The correspondences of each cosmic factor should be arranged together into a total picture and the meaning of the individual components combined into a coordinated whole. Users repeatedly confirm the often quite disconcerting agreement between some of the interpretations as given and the characteristics and events of an individual's life. But in this very fact there is a danger. A statement must be confirmed not just once but many times and repeatedly if it is to be brought to a level of certainty upon which one can base defensible diagnosis or prognosis. Moreover, one should not neglect to take into account the present conditions of the individual, his or her stage of development, age, environment, walk of life and other factors, and to combine all of these considerations with the findings from the birth chart. The cosmic factor alone is never sufficient, nor ever can be. Since the 1950 edition numerous advances have been made in cosmobiology which increasingly accentuate the difference between it and the type of "soothsaying" that is so often practiced in the name of astrology. Many particulars have been thoroughly worked out, conclusive statements evolved and work made easier and rationalized with suitable modem methods. The advantages of the 90-degree-circle have been increasingly recognized so that now no skilled practitioners would consider themselves capable of making a reliable diagnosis or prognosis without it. After World War II, Reinhold Ebertin developed a new method of charting (K2) which combines the 90° and the usual 360° systems on one comprehensive chart form. We may note here in connection with illustrations E/l and E/2, that the 90° circle is placed round the outside of the usual 360° zodiac. The first 30° contain the cardinal signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; 60o-90o the mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. This means that when the positions are marked on the 90° circle, conjunction, square and opposition aspects all fall together and the semisquare and sesquiquadrate aspects fall opposite. Thus when several positions fall together one can see at once which factors are in relationship to each other. For example, here in E/2, Jupiter, Neptune, Ascendant and Mars form such a complex. The full advantages of this system only become really apparent when one is working with transits and directions. In this connection attention is drawn to Angewandte Kosmobiologie {Applied Cosmobiology). A further help is Gesicherte Schnelldiagnose {Certain, Quick Diagnosis), which shows the way in which the combinations in a chart will work out. The cosmic state of a stellar body is determined from a synthesis of its various aspects and mid-point-combinations. It can be very quickly determined with the aid of the 90o-circle. Example E/2 is the chart of the Italian racing cyclist Fausto Coppi. In example E/3, only the cosmic state of Mars has been drawn in. Mars lies in the mid-points Moon/MC and Sun/Pluto. (In precise work with mid-points an orb of only 1V20 should be allowed.) It should also be remembered that one speaks of "indirect mid-points" when a factor is not actually on the mid-point axis itself but at a 45° angle to this axis. In this case Mars is almost exactly at the mid-point, or axis, of Sun/Pluto and 45° from the Moon/MC axis. • Mars = Moon/MC: "The devotion to a task or cause both in body and soul... industriousness, the urge to strive constantly for the fulfillment of an objective. .. ." • Mars = Sun/Pluto: "The desire to perform record achievements ... over exertion or overtaxing ones powers.. .. The tendency to work until physical breakdown occurs." These statements certainly correspond with the character of a racing cyclist. The cosmic states such as in example E/3 and in the examples that follow are delineated as part of a "structural-picture" or as "structural-elements." Structural-element is a term synonymous with cosmic state. The structural picture is the "picture" in which all the structural-elements of the chart are contained. The great value of the structural-elements lies in the fact that they are open to comparison in different charts, as will be shown in detail later. However one can only compare charts adequately when they have been erected by a fixed system. Most types of horoscopes in use do not lend themselves to easy comparison as the horizon is usually drawn horizontally across the chart X "J** A. TlLn $ <5" + 32, Ex. E/l % Ex. E/2 va/ and the MC vertically or obliquely to it. The value of the individual positioning of each picture is well established, but only its zodiacal positioning. As the Sun is at its highest position in Cancer, 0° Cancer is placed at the top of the chart and this marks the zero point of the 90°-circle, as is shown in E/2 and E/3. When drawing up the structural-picture we further simplify things. The factor under examination (Mars in this case) is set down, a vertical line is drawn under it, and the individual mid-points grouped round it as is shown in E/4. Groupings of other factors are seen round E/3. The strict order of some of the positions has been changed around but it in fact seems to be unimportant whether Mars is in the middle of Moon/MC or MC/Moon. Experience has shown that for the most part the important thing is which factors are combined, while it often seems to be of less importance how these factors are actually grouped. Examples of this are given later. To illustrate this further the structural-elements (cosmic-states) of Jupiter, Pluto and Moon, examples E/5-E/7, have been added. By comparing the structural-elements of different charts it is possible to replace earlier dogmatic, artificial and inspired "interpretations" with reliable, scientifically established statements. The cosmo-psychogram was developed jointly by Reinhold and Dr. Baldur Ebertin. Its basis is explained in detail and substantiated with numerous illustrations in Die kosmischen Grundlagen unseres Lebens. Its use pre-dates the introduction of structural-elements in chart analysis and in setting up the cosmo-psychogram somewhat larger orbs are used for aspects. Examples E/8 and E/9 show two quite dissimilar cosmo-psychograms. The cosmo-psychogram shows in the form of a seventeen rayed diagram the results obtained by evaluating the structural-elements of a chart according to a fixed key. The bottom four rays show the individual's "type-composition," i.e., the proportion of tension and relaxation, and of inward and outward interest (the tendency to introversion or extroversion). The type-composition is based upon the sign positions of the individual horoscopic factors. The middle circle of the cosmo-psychogram shows the distance-value of each heavenly body. This is based upon its distance from the Earth, from value 0 for apogee to 100 at perigee. Each of the 13 birth chart factors is represented by a ray on the cosmo-psychogram. The white inner portion of each ray is its positive value and the black outer portion its negative value. The length of the ray is determined by evaluating the factors mid-points and aspects according to a fixed key. The total white section is defined as the positive "kernel" and the total black section as the negative "mantle." If we compare the two cases E/8 and E/9, it is immediately apparent that in E/8 there is a very large positive kernel and a weak negative mantle, while in E/9 on the other hand there is a smaller positive kernel and a very much larger negative mantle. Furthermore, while E/8 gives an unbroken and coherent impression E/9 appears ragged and disjointed. The actual case histories of these two cases are as follows; E/8 is the psycho-cosmogram of a "happy and successful woman" who has always achieved her aims in life and prospered, while E/9 is the psycho-cosmogram of an extremely sickly individual. He was a forceps delivery and has suffered paralysis since birth and has had to spend his life in a home for the handicapped. Anyone who thoroughly studies cosmo-psychograms will find confirmation of their excellence as tools for the scientific comparison of birth charts. A comparable basis has been developed for use in prognosis: the "years-curve." By evaluating planetary transits according to a fixed key it is possible to represent them in the form of a curve. The curve is drawn about a base line which is divided into months as shown in example E/10. This is part of the years-curve for the late J. F. Dulles. The curve shows a positive high in the autumn of 1958 as Dulles, the then U.S. minister for external affairs, made his successful visit to the Near East. At the beginning of 1959, the curve descends steeply. As the curve crossed the base line in February 1959, Dulles was hospitalized. He died when the curve reached its lowest point in late May. Full instructions and examples can be found in Die Jahreskurve. The 450graph-ephemerides are another useful tool. By their use it is possible to survey any particular period in a very short time and to quickly compare the transiting configurations in different charts. Examples E/10 and E/l 1 show extracts from the graphs of two women who were bom on the same day in different years and who suffered still births within two weeks of each other. Comparative Research After this survey of some of the progress that has been made in our subject during the last decade the author would particularly like to introduce the concept of comparative research in order that it may encourage more practical work in this field. In the case of family research it is exceptionally interesting to compare the structural-elements in the charts of the different members of a family. In example E/13, which is taken from Kosmobiologie, Vol. 25, Feb. 1959, the structural-elements of two children and their parents are set out in a form that has not hitherto been used. By arranging the structural-elements of each chart in rows one under another it is possible to determine similarities and to mark these in more strongly. Although it is generally believed that blood transfusions cannot damage the physical character and mental predispositions of the recipient of the blood, it has however been found at times that damage can be caused. In the case given it was established that the Rhesus factor was of importance. The incompatibility of this factor between mother and child can have serious consequences for the child. After the birth of her first child on February 15, 1939, the mother received daily blood transfusions for a whole week as she had had a severe hemorrhage. When this happens it has been found that it presents a special danger for the second child. Seven years later a second child was bom. After birth he became ill with severe jaundice. Eighteen months later the child had to be admitted to hospital following the diagnosis of a deterioration in the red blood corpuscles. One may note in E/13 that the two children share a common structural-element: Sun = Neptune/Pluto and MC/Pluto. In one case the MC is found with Pluto and in the other with Neptune. It may however be accepted that the parents already had a predisposition to this condition. It is known that the father contacted poliomyelitis at the age of four. One observes that the same combinations, but in a different form, occur in the case of the parents. Each of their Neptune structural-elements contains the mid-point Sun/Pluto. Other similarities to be found in this case are: AS = Venus/Mars, AS = Jupiter/Saturn, Mars = Moon/Pluto, Mars = Satum/AS, Saturn = Moon/Venus, Uranus = Saturn/Pluto, Pluto = Moon/Neptune etc. It is known that cosmic factors are inherited. However, the number of similarities found in this case is not likely to be met with very often. In the case of illnesses one should always consider the Biological Correspondence sections in this book. It is still too early, however, to be able to give precise methods for medical diagnosis from the chart. In no case should one be tempted to make a diagnosis on the basis of cosmic factors alone. It would be irresponsible for anyone to make a medical diagnosis on this basis without taking a doctor into consultation to corroborate one's findings. Such examinations can only be a means of help to medicine but can never be by itself the basis for a diagnosis. A further case of blood disease is found in examples E/14 and E/15, from Kosmobiologie, Vol. 28, April 1961. The child was confirmed to have a progressive deterioration of the blood in its seventh year. Here again mother and child have a similar combination involving Neptune-Pluto-Sun, while they also reveal a second common structural-elements involving variations on Sun-Neptune-Satum. In the five cases of poliomyelitis given, the first five cases from our polio research file, we may observe once again that each example contains the combination Sun-Neptune-Pluto in some form or another. We may remember that the same structural-elements were found in the case of the father in E/l 3 who had had polio. We cannot of course say yet that in cases of blood disease and poliomyelitis that this stellar combination will always be present, especially as the contraction of polio has not really been explained yet. Through the mutual cooperation of cosmobiologists it may be possible to institute cosmobiology as a tool for the diagnosis of disease. If this is to be accomplished it is necessarily of the first importance to work in conjunction with the medical profession. Next to health the question of success in life is considered by most people to be of particular importance. The question is constantly asked in vocational guidance as to whether the chart already contains the particular predispositions necessary for especial success. In the following examples it will become evident that successful individuals and those responsible for great undertakings do have similar structural-elements in their charts. The great industrialist Dr. Friedrich Flick is the son of a farmer and mines timber merchant. He obtained a diploma in retail trading, by the age of twenty-four was already a confidential clerk, and by thirty was head of a steel company. Today he is one of the richest industrialists, holding shares in numerous companies, such as Daimler-Benz, Monopol-Bergbau and Auto-Union. Bertgikd Beitz is the son of a bank official. He had to earn his school fees by giving private tuition. He went on to study banking and by twenty-four was head of a bank. He was exempted from military service and put in charge of the exploitation of the Polish oil fields. Later he met Alfried Krupp and is today the head of Krupps. Herbert Ekloh comes from a family of grocers. He himself managed a small shop until he had saved enough money to travel to the U.S. From there he returned with many new ideas and acted as an adviser to a group of chain stores. He then started his first self-service shops and was unusually successful. In all of these successful men we find Sun/Jupiter = Mars, which is the ability to succeed. In the case of Flick, this combination is made particularly important by the addition of Pluto, while his success in cooperation with others by Moon's Node = Sun/Mars and Sun/Pluto. In the case of Beitz, Mars is in the mid-points both of Sun/Jupiter and Jupiter/Pluto. In the case of Ekloh, he also has Jupiter = Sun/Pluto, another combination for success. Naturally many other combinations are of importance in these charts but they cannot all be mentioned here. Sigorsky invented the first helicopter as a model when he was still a child. He built the first four-engine airplane in the world and later on became known as "the master of the impossible." Tupolew began his career by building gliders. In the last few years he has caused a considerable stir with his 200-seat TU114, which has four turbo-prop engines and a range of 5,000 miles. In the case of the inventor of the atomic submarine, Hyman G. Rickover, the Mercury-Uranus axis lies in the success mid-point Jupiter/Pluto. Felix Wankel, inventor of the Wankel-engine, has the same factors in combination but differently arranged. Hall and Heroult both discovered aluminum. They were bom in the same year and made their discoveries in the same year but completely independently. Both cases contain similar structural-elements, of which Neptune = Mars/Jupiter is of special interest as the discovery of Neptune heralded the period in which chemistry came to the forefront and has been considered as the planet associated with chemistry. The one-time president of the people's court of justice, Dr. Roland Freisler, was originally a communist and a commissar in a Russian prisoner-of-war camp before he acquired the reputation as a fanatical and ruthless judge who handed down innumerable death sentences. One could interpret the planetary picture given in E/54 as success (Jupiter/Pluto) through mass (Moon's Node) murder (Mars/Saturn). The advantages of this method of presentation in terms of structural-elements and structural-pictures will be obvious. Looking for similarities in charts erected in the usual manner is extremely tedious. It is assumed, however, that in converting the chart into its 90° form that the 90o-disc is used which enables one to also see the 360° chart. The interrelationships of the 360° should not be neglected, whilst an even better overall assessment of the chart can be obtained from the use of the cosmo-psychogram. General Remarks The observation and research of illness requires a great deal of care and tact. The author has been particularly careful in all of his statements. No-one should be tempted to give a diagnosis on the basis of the cosmic picture alone because it is impossible. So many factors add to the situation which is shown in the chart, but which can only be released under special circumstances. These cannot be foreseen from the chart. One should always consider that Biological Correspondences are based on cooperation with doctors. The Biological Correspondences can become effective through various circumstances. One must always be very careful in interpreting disease. Those who work on cosmobiology must be constantly aware that it is nonsense to read the destiny from the stars alone. It is also important to have some knowledge of psychology and medicine and a rich experience of life if one wants to help not only one's own family but others too. With every word spoken by the cosmoblological investigator one should be conscious of the responsibility and the damaging consequences which the wrong words could have. One does not help others by making them afraid of the future but must use every opportunity to build up their self-confidence and their self-consciousness of their own value. Those who advise others should always remember that it is not for them to bring about a decision in the life of another. It is for the cosmobiologist to give help and build up confidence in others so that they can make their own decisions to the best of their ability. Translator's Notes Since the appearance of the first English edition in 1960, The Combination of Stellar Influences has universally established itself as a standard work of outstanding importance. In preparing this translation of the 1961 supplement we have followed Dr. Roosedale's translation of technical terms wherever appropriate, e.g., "Gestim" has been translated as "stellar body" to refer equally to planet, Sun or Moon. Likewise, quotations from the main body of the text have always been given as they appear in the original translation. As many readers may be as yet unfamiliar with the 90o-circle method of charting described in this supplement, it should be mentioned that this method is usually employed in conjunction with a 90o-dial. This is a simple instrument which enables one to examine all the mid-point axes in a chart in a few minutes. It is an absolutely essential tool for work in this field. Meanwhile it is hoped that this supplementary material will further stimulate research along the lines pioneered by Mr, Ebertin. Charles Harvey Use Hodges May 1969 It has always been the intention that the individual statements given in The Combination of Stellar Influences should only be used as suggestions for the interpretation of the combinations and never as though they were immutable and finally established rules. The correspondences of each cosmic factor should be arranged together into a total picture and the meaning of the individual components combined into a coordinated whole. Users repeatedly confirm the often quite disconcerting agreement between some of the interpretations as given and the characteristics and events of an individual's life. But in this very fact there is a danger. A statement must be confirmed not just once but many times and repeatedly if it is to be brought to a level of certainty upon which one can base defensible diagnosis or prognosis. Moreover, one should not neglect to take into account the present conditions of the individual, his or her stage of development, age, environment, walk of life and other factors, and to combine all of these considerations with the findings from the birth chart. The cosmic factor alone is never sufficient, nor ever can be. Since the 1950 edition numerous advances have been made in cosmobiology which increasingly accentuate the difference between it and the type of "soothsaying" that is so often practiced in the name of astrology. Many particulars have been thoroughly worked out, conclusive statements evolved and work made easier and rationalized with suitable modem methods. The advantages of the 90-degree-circle have been increasingly recognized so that now no skilled practitioners would consider themselves capable of making a reliable diagnosis or prognosis without it. After World War II, Reinhold Ebertin developed a new method of charting (K2) which combines the 90° and the usual 360° systems on one comprehensive chart form. We may note here in connection with illustrations E/l and E/2, that the 90° circle is placed round the outside of the usual 360° zodiac. The first 30° contain the cardinal signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; 60o-90o the mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. This means that when the positions are marked on the 90° circle, conjunction, square and opposition aspects all fall together and the semisquare and sesquiquadrate aspects fall opposite. Thus when several positions fall together one can see at once which factors are in relationship to each other. For example, here in E/2, Jupiter, Neptune, Ascendant and Mars form such a complex. The full advantages of this system only become really apparent when one is working with transits and directions. In this connection attention is drawn to Angewandte Kosmobiologie {Applied Cosmobiology). A further help is Gesicherte Schnelldiagnose {Certain, Quick Diagnosis), which shows the way in which the combinations in a chart will work out. The cosmic state of a stellar body is determined from a synthesis of its various aspects and mid-point-combinations. It can be very quickly determined with the aid of the 90o-circle. Example E/2 is the chart of the Italian racing cyclist Fausto Coppi. In example E/3, only the cosmic state of Mars has been drawn in. Mars lies in the mid-points Moon/MC and Sun/Pluto. (In precise work with mid-points an orb of only 1V20 should be allowed.) It should also be remembered that one speaks of "indirect mid-points" when a factor is not actually on the mid-point axis itself but at a 45° angle to this axis. In this case Mars is almost exactly at the mid-point, or axis, of Sun/Pluto and 45° from the Moon/MC axis. • Mars = Moon/MC: "The devotion to a task or cause both in body and soul... industriousness, the urge to strive constantly for the fulfillment of an objective. .. ." • Mars = Sun/Pluto: "The desire to perform record achievements ... over exertion or overtaxing ones powers.. .. The tendency to work until physical breakdown occurs." These statements certainly correspond with the character of a racing cyclist. The cosmic states such as in example E/3 and in the examples that follow are delineated as part of a "structural-picture" or as "structural-elements." Structural-element is a term synonymous with cosmic state. The structural picture is the "picture" in which all the structural-elements of the chart are contained. The great value of the structural-elements lies in the fact that they are open to comparison in different charts, as will be shown in detail later. However one can only compare charts adequately when they have been erected by a fixed system. Most types of horoscopes in use do not lend themselves to easy comparison as the horizon is usually drawn horizontally across the chart X "J** A. TlLn $ <5" + 32, Ex. E/l % Ex. E/2 va/ and the MC vertically or obliquely to it. The value of the individual positioning of each picture is well established, but only its zodiacal positioning. As the Sun is at its highest position in Cancer, 0° Cancer is placed at the top of the chart and this marks the zero point of the 90°-circle, as is shown in E/2 and E/3. When drawing up the structural-picture we further simplify things. The factor under examination (Mars in this case) is set down, a vertical line is drawn under it, and the individual mid-points grouped round it as is shown in E/4. Groupings of other factors are seen round E/3. The strict order of some of the positions has been changed around but it in fact seems to be unimportant whether Mars is in the middle of Moon/MC or MC/Moon. Experience has shown that for the most part the important thing is which factors are combined, while it often seems to be of less importance how these factors are actually grouped. Examples of this are given later. To illustrate this further the structural-elements (cosmic-states) of Jupiter, Pluto and Moon, examples E/5-E/7, have been added. By comparing the structural-elements of different charts it is possible to replace earlier dogmatic, artificial and inspired "interpretations" with reliable, scientifically established statements. The cosmo-psychogram was developed jointly by Reinhold and Dr. Baldur Ebertin. Its basis is explained in detail and substantiated with numerous illustrations in Die kosmischen Grundlagen unseres Lebens. Its use pre-dates the introduction of structural-elements in chart analysis and in setting up the cosmo-psychogram somewhat larger orbs are used for aspects. Examples E/8 and E/9 show two quite dissimilar cosmo-psychograms. The cosmo-psychogram shows in the form of a seventeen rayed diagram the results obtained by evaluating the structural-elements of a chart according to a fixed key. The bottom four rays show the individual's "type-composition," i.e., the proportion of tension and relaxation, and of inward and outward interest (the tendency to introversion or extroversion). The type-composition is based upon the sign positions of the individual horoscopic factors. The middle circle of the cosmo-psychogram shows the distance-value of each heavenly body. This is based upon its distance from the Earth, from value 0 for apogee to 100 at perigee. Each of the 13 birth chart factors is represented by a ray on the cosmo-psychogram. The white inner portion of each ray is its positive value and the black outer portion its negative value. The length of the ray is determined by evaluating the factors mid-points and aspects according to a fixed key. The total white section is defined as the positive "kernel" and the total black section as the negative "mantle." If we compare the two cases E/8 and E/9, it is immediately apparent that in E/8 there is a very large positive kernel and a weak negative mantle, while in E/9 on the other hand there is a smaller positive kernel and a very much larger negative mantle. Furthermore, while E/8 gives an unbroken and coherent impression E/9 appears ragged and disjointed. The actual case histories of these two cases are as follows; E/8 is the psycho-cosmogram of a "happy and successful woman" who has always achieved her aims in life and prospered, while E/9 is the psycho-cosmogram of an extremely sickly individual. He was a forceps delivery and has suffered paralysis since birth and has had to spend his life in a home for the handicapped. Anyone who thoroughly studies cosmo-psychograms will find confirmation of their excellence as tools for the scientific comparison of birth charts. A comparable basis has been developed for use in prognosis: the "years-curve." By evaluating planetary transits according to a fixed key it is possible to represent them in the form of a curve. The curve is drawn about a base line which is divided into months as shown in example E/10. This is part of the years-curve for the late J. F. Dulles. The curve shows a positive high in the autumn of 1958 as Dulles, the then U.S. minister for external affairs, made his successful visit to the Near East. At the beginning of 1959, the curve descends steeply. As the curve crossed the base line in February 1959, Dulles was hospitalized. He died when the curve reached its lowest point in late May. Full instructions and examples can be found in Die Jahreskurve. The 450graph-ephemerides are another useful tool. By their use it is possible to survey any particular period in a very short time and to quickly compare the transiting configurations in different charts. Examples E/10 and E/l 1 show extracts from the graphs of two women who were bom on the same day in different years and who suffered still births within two weeks of each other. Comparative Research After this survey of some of the progress that has been made in our subject during the last decade the author would particularly like to introduce the concept of comparative research in order that it may encourage more practical work in this field. In the case of family research it is exceptionally interesting to compare the structural-elements in the charts of the different members of a family. In example E/13, which is taken from Kosmobiologie, Vol. 25, Feb. 1959, the structural-elements of two children and their parents are set out in a form that has not hitherto been used. By arranging the structural-elements of each chart in rows one under another it is possible to determine similarities and to mark these in more strongly. Although it is generally believed that blood transfusions cannot damage the physical character and mental predispositions of the recipient of the blood, it has however been found at times that damage can be caused. In the case given it was established that the Rhesus factor was of importance. The incompatibility of this factor between mother and child can have serious consequences for the child. After the birth of her first child on February 15, 1939, the mother received daily blood transfusions for a whole week as she had had a severe hemorrhage. When this happens it has been found that it presents a special danger for the second child. Seven years later a second child was bom. After birth he became ill with severe jaundice. Eighteen months later the child had to be admitted to hospital following the diagnosis of a deterioration in the red blood corpuscles. One may note in E/13 that the two children share a common structural-element: Sun = Neptune/Pluto and MC/Pluto. In one case the MC is found with Pluto and in the other with Neptune. It may however be accepted that the parents already had a predisposition to this condition. It is known that the father contacted poliomyelitis at the age of four. One observes that the same combinations, but in a different form, occur in the case of the parents. Each of their Neptune structural-elements contains the mid-point Sun/Pluto. Other similarities to be found in this case are: AS = Venus/Mars, AS = Jupiter/Saturn, Mars = Moon/Pluto, Mars = Satum/AS, Saturn = Moon/Venus, Uranus = Saturn/Pluto, Pluto = Moon/Neptune etc. It is known that cosmic factors are inherited. However, the number of similarities found in this case is not likely to be met with very often. In the case of illnesses one should always consider the Biological Correspondence sections in this book. It is still too early, however, to be able to give precise methods for medical diagnosis from the chart. In no case should one be tempted to make a diagnosis on the basis of cosmic factors alone. It would be irresponsible for anyone to make a medical diagnosis on this basis without taking a doctor into consultation to corroborate one's findings. Such examinations can only be a means of help to medicine but can never be by itself the basis for a diagnosis. A further case of blood disease is found in examples E/14 and E/15, from Kosmobiologie, Vol. 28, April 1961. The child was confirmed to have a progressive deterioration of the blood in its seventh year. Here again mother and child have a similar combination involving Neptune-Pluto-Sun, while they also reveal a second common structural-elements involving variations on Sun-Neptune-Satum. In the five cases of poliomyelitis given, the first five cases from our polio research file, we may observe once again that each example contains the combination Sun-Neptune-Pluto in some form or another. We may remember that the same structural-elements were found in the case of the father in E/l 3 who had had polio. We cannot of course say yet that in cases of blood disease and poliomyelitis that this stellar combination will always be present, especially as the contraction of polio has not really been explained yet. If this is to be accomplished it is necessarily of the first importance to work in conjunction with the medical profession. Next to health the question of success in life is considered by most people to be of particular importance. The question is constantly asked in vocational guidance as to whether the chart already contains the particular predispositions necessary for especial success. In the following examples it will become evident that successful individuals and those responsible for great undertakings do have similar structural-elements in their charts. The great industrialist Dr. Friedrich Flick is the son of a farmer and mines timber merchant. He obtained a diploma in retail trading, by the age of twenty-four was already a confidential clerk, and by thirty was head of a steel company. Today he is one of the richest industrialists, holding shares in numerous companies, such as Daimler-Benz, Monopol-Bergbau and Auto-Union. Bertgikd Beitz is the son of a bank official. He had to earn his school fees by giving private tuition. He went on to study banking and by twenty-four was head of a bank. He was exempted from military service and put in charge of the exploitation of the Polish oil fields. Later he met Alfried Krupp and is today the head of Krupps. Herbert Ekloh comes from a family of grocers. He himself managed a small shop until he had saved enough money to travel to the U.S. From there he returned with many new ideas and acted as an adviser to a group of chain stores. He then started his first self-service shops and was unusually successful. In all of these successful men we find Sun/Jupiter = Mars, which is the ability to succeed. In the case of Flick, this combination is made particularly important by the addition of Pluto, while his success in cooperation with others by Moon's Node = Sun/Mars and Sun/Pluto. In the case of Beitz, Mars is in the mid-points both of Sun/Jupiter and Jupiter/Pluto. In the case of Ekloh, he also has Jupiter = Sun/Pluto, another combination for success. Naturally many other combinations are of importance in these charts but they cannot all be mentioned here. native_text:
Psychic sensitivity, which can manifest in irrational fear, paranoia, feeling drained, confused, etc. The need to take one’s psychic sensitivity seriously, and to protect it. Physical problems whose roots are to be found in one’s psychic sensitivity, and which can therefore be difficult to diagnose by traditional medical means. The attempt to combine the ideal with the real, that is, to bring one’s ideals into physical manifestation. The feeling of being let down, frustrated, or sad when one’s ideals fail to become a reality. The need to stand firm and true by one’s ideals and to purify them by purging them of any delusions or distortions, so that one may clearly see the relation ship between one’s hopes and dreams and physical reality.

The clearing away of confusion and misconceptions. The realization of the relationship between one’s ideals and the limitations of the physical world, which leads to the ability to hold on to ideals while yet also being able to live them in some practi cal, real way. The breaking down of old, worn out and/or needlessly limiting structures.

A compelling need to connect to positive energy and to spirit guides. An urgent need to clear past karmas and to resolve issues of the past so that one can move forward. A need to understand one’s attachments to the past and how those attachments are fear-based. Needing to seek out people who are willing to grow and evolve with oneself. A need to connect with people who will accept the love one has to give. Tension between oneself and others caused by others unwillingness to grow or change. Often the source of this tension is hidden. Sometimes one has great problems with others that are hard to define. The only way to solve these problems is to trust in one’s instincts and to be receptive to answers coming from deep inside oneself or from spirit guides.

The finding of ways to evolve, often ways one does not expect and which turn out to be short-cuts that speed the process of the growth of consciousness.
